title: Equations of Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
seo_title: Geometry Equations of Parallel and Perpendicular Lines Worksheets (TEKS G.2C)
standard_text: G.2C determine an equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheets for Texas TEKS G.2C: parallel and perpendicular slopes and equations of parallel and perpendicular lines through a point. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: opposite reciprocal.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Parallel lines: same slope.
  • Perpendicular lines: slopes are opposite reciprocals (their product is −1).
  • Use the slope and the point in y − y1 = m(x − x1), then simplify.

Examples

Example

Parallel to y = 3x − 1 through (2, 4)

4 = 3(2) + b

b = −2

Answer: y = 3x − 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Same slope for perpendicular linesFlip and change the sign.
Not changing the signPerpendicular to 2 is −1/2.
Using x as the interceptSolve for b.

faq.a: Determine an equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point.

faq.q: What is perpendicular to a horizontal line?
What is the product of perpendicular slopes?
Do parallel lines have the same y-intercept?
faq.a: No, or they would be the same line.

items.q: A line passes through (−5, 3) and (−7, −1). What is the slope of a line parallel to it?
items.e: Slope = (−1 − 3) ÷ (−7 − (−5)) = 2. Parallel lines have the same slope: 2.
